== Problem ==

The table below shows the ancient Egyptian hieroglyphs that were used to represent different numbers.

[[File:mathh.PNG]]

For example, the number <imath>32</imath> was represented by the hieroglyphs <imath>\cap \cap \cap ||</imath>. What number is represented by the following combination of hieroglyphs?

[[File:Amc8 2025 prob 2 pic.PNG]]

<imath>\textbf{(A)}\ 1,423 \qquad \textbf{(B)}\ 10,423 \qquad \textbf{(C)}\ 14,023 \qquad \textbf{(D)}\ 14,203 \qquad \textbf{(E)}\ 14,230</imath>

== Solution 1 ==

The first hieroglyph is worth <imath>10,000</imath>, the next 4 are worth <imath>100 \cdot 4 = 400</imath>, the next <imath>2</imath> are worth <imath>10 \cdot 2 = 20</imath>, and the last <imath>3</imath> are worth <imath>1 \cdot 3 = 3</imath>. Therefore, the answer is <imath>10,000 + 400 + 20 + 3 = \boxed{\textbf{(B)}\ 10,423}</imath>

== Solution 2 ==
\( 1 \cdot 10^4 + 0 \cdot 10^3 + 4 \cdot 10^2 + 2 \cdot 10^1 + 3 \cdot 10^0 = 10423 \)

== Solution 3 (fast version of Solution x) ==

From a first inspection, you may notice that there is no thousands hieroglyph. The only option with zero in the thousands place is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(B)}\ 10,423}</imath>
